tunnel.note: The SOLIT2 test gallery AS TESTED. This is the standard, not a project. Annex 2 section 2 'Test Tunnel' (p.5) states the geometry outright: 'The tunnel has a length of 600 m with a slope of 1%. The width of the original tunnel is 9,5 m with a height of 8,20 m. To perform fire tests with semi-transversal ventilation and to protect the tunnel, some modifications were made prior to the test program. Over a length of 450 m a suspended ceiling with a height of 5,20 m was installed. Furthermore, in the surrounding of the fire area, additional walls were installed to provide a tunnel with of 7,50 m.' THIS IS A MODIFIED SECTION, NOT A NATURAL BORE: the 5.20 m height is a SUSPENDED CEILING over 450 m of a tunnel that is 8.20 m high underneath it, and the 7.50 m width comes from WALLS ADDED around the fire area inside a bore that is 9.5 m wide. The as-tested cross-section is therefore 7.50 x 5.20 m, 39.0 m2, which is what the c4/c5/c6 reference cases were measured in. This preset previously carried 9.5 m x 5.17 m / 48 m2: the 9.5 m was the ORIGINAL unmodified width and the 5.17 m matched nothing in Annex 2. clearance_m 4.5 is NOT stated anywhere in Annex 2 and is unverified against the source. Also from the same Annex 2 section, and not representable in this schema: the tunnel has 6 jet fans giving a maximum longitudinal air velocity of 6.5 m/s, and its semi-transversal system 'is designed to deal with free burning fires of approx. 30 MW'. Annex 7 5.2.6 puts the fire target 5 m downstream of the mock-up, of the same width, height and combustibility. Annex 7 5.2.7 mandates that BOTH 1.5 m/s and 3.0 m/s longitudinal velocity be tested, measured 45 m upstream of the fire -- a velocity range is a property of the TEST, not of the tunnel, so it is not carried here: see the designs under examples/designs/, which set ventilation.velocity_range_ms to [1.5, 3.0] so the envelope actually runs both. These are TEST conditions, not site conditions; Annex 7 3.3 governs transferring results between them.

fire.note: The Annex 7 Class A HGV mock-up. Section 5.2.1 sets a minimum potential HRR of 150 MW unsuppressed, and section 5.2.2 the geometry: 'Height: Minimum 4,0m (having minimum 2,5m height for the fuel part) / Width: 2,4m / Length: 10,0m', with 'A minimum of 400 pallets corresponding to a minimum HGV design fire size of approximately 110-140 GJ'. base_height_m 1.5 is that section's own arithmetic, not an assumption: a minimum 4.0 m total height carrying a minimum 2.5 m fuel part puts the trailer platform at 4.0 - 2.5 = 1.5 m. The 10.0 m length is what makes section 6.3's station identity hold -- 'the ends of the HGV Class A mock-up are located in U5 and D5. Correspondingly the fire target is located at D10'. lane_centre_offset_from_wall_m follows section 5.2.3: 'The mock-up shall be eccentric to the centre line of the test tunnel. The distance from the side wall shall be less than 1,5 m', measured by Figure 8/Figure 13 from the near face, so 2.5 - 2.4/2 = 1.3 m of wall clearance. Annex 7 rejects the centred position because it flatters the system: 'such a position is often most effective for FFFS since the fire fighting medium is properly delivered on both sides'.

nozzles.note: PLACEHOLDER -- NOT the real SOLIT2 test-system nozzle. Confirmed 2026-09-27 against the primary source (SOLIT2 Engineering Guidance Annex 2, http://www.solit.info/PDF/SOLIT_EG_Annex2_EN_v2.1.pdf) that SOLIT2 does not publish the reference test system's nozzle hydraulics anywhere: Annex 2 section 4.1.3 lists 'Type of the nozzle (Shape, K-factor, etc.)' only as a category of layout parameter that 'corresponded to the real installation in the tunnel' and never gives a value; no manufacturer or model is named. No public document exists to source this from. Every value below is instead taken from Mistelix's OWN nozzle datasheet (MTX-WMS-NOZ-DS-001 Rev 1, 2026-09-21, Part B MTX-REV01P proposal) as a mechanical stand-in ONLY, to exercise the refit pipeline -- it is a different nozzle, from a different manufacturer, entered here only because no real SOLIT2 reference-nozzle data exists to enter. That datasheet states explicitly 'no Mistelix nozzle measured' -- every number is ESTIMATED (Merrington-Richardson/Elkotb correlations, Rosin-Rammler spread q=2.5 assumed) or read from CAD, none measured. Per instruction, the LOWEST value at each point was taken: the C_d=0.673 measured-hole bound (itself only a client test-hole datum of unconfirmed provenance, DS-01 Q-041) rather than the 0.78 literature bound, at the lowest tabulated pressure (35 bar, the NFPA750 floor is 34.5). mounting.rows/pitch_m/row_lateral_offsets_m have no source in this datasheet at all -- it documents a single nozzle's hydraulics, not a test-rig's row layout -- and are pure schema-required filler with no physical meaning (rows=1, pitch_m=1.0, one offset of 0.0). height_above_carriageway_m=4.6 and tilt_deg=35 are the datasheet's one stated install note ('35 deg below horizontal, wall-mounted at 4.6 m'); note this schema's mounting.type is fixed to ceiling_rows, so the datasheet's actual wall-mounted geometry does not fit this model either. Any refit or validate output produced against this file is NOT a validated SOLIT2 calibration and must not be reported as one.
